sidebar.title: Action Economy
sidebar.p: At the start of every combat turn, each player receives 5 Action Points (APs) and 1 Out-of-Turn Action.

Characters can spend their APs on their turn to perform actions orchecks by subtracting the AP Cost of the check from their remaining APs. If the character does not have enough APs remaining to pay the AP Cost of the check, then they cannot attempt that check.
Characters can spend their OOTA to perform certain checks on someone elses turn. There are three types of OOTAs:

description.p: are Counterchecks that require the use of an Out-of-Turn Action for example: Dodge, Parry, and Shield Block. The Out-of-Turn Action is used when the counter check is chosen. If the character has no remaining Out-of-Turn actions then they must choose a Countercheck that does not require one, Armor.
are Out-of-Turn actions whose effects occur before the effects of the current action. Usually interrupts will have a set of preconditions that must be met before they can be triggered.
are like Interrupts but their effects occur after the effects of the current action are applied.
